After staging everything we move on to the mart layer (dims & facts) so that we can analyze the dashboard fast.
<!--
We are creating data mart to organize our staged data.
The marts are indexed, aggregated, and structure for faster joins.
These marts induce clarity as they reflect business language (Sales, purchases, vendors)

This pattern is what we call star Schema, ( facts are in the center and dimensions surround them ). It is the foundation of analytics engineering (DBT, snowflake etc. )
    1. Facts are measurable events
    2. Dimensions are descriptive context
    3. Grain is well defined
        - fact sales: daily/store/product
        - fact purchases: PO/product
        - fact inventory: snapshot date/store/product
    4. Goal is to create business ready models for dashboards, KPIs and Analytics.
 -->

```{sql}
Create schema if not exists mart;


```

<!--
Describing dimensions and facts.
    1. Dimension tables store descriptive attributes ( the "who, what, where, when");
        dim_product= brand, description, size
        dim_store= location details.
        dim_vendor= supplier info.
        dim_date= calendar attributes (month, year, weekend flag)
    2. fact tables store measured events (the " how much , when "
        fct_sales= quantity, dollars sold, by date/store/product.
        fct_purchases= PO quantities & costs, by vendor/product
        fct_inventory_snapshot= how much stock existed on a given day.
    This is what allows easy slicing and dicing of data (what we are studying in MGTA452)
    ex-> show sales dollars by brand in city in Q4= join facts to product, store and date dims.
        Here is where the indexes help too.
            Facts can have millions of rows. Indexes on dates, product_id, vendor_id make filters and joins fast. and we only add indexes on common joins because this ensures we are getting the perfomance gain without having overhead.

 -->
1. Dimensions
    1.1 dim date (from our date ranges)
```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.dim_date;
CREATE TABLE mart.dim_date AS
WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT
    LEAST(
      (SELECT MIN(sales_date)     FROM stg.sales),
      (SELECT MIN(po_date)        FROM stg.purchases),
      (SELECT MIN(start_date)     FROM stg.begin_inventory),
      (SELECT MIN(end_date)       FROM stg.end_inventory)
    ) AS dmin,
    GREATEST(
      (SELECT MAX(sales_date)     FROM stg.sales),
      (SELECT MAX(receiving_date) FROM stg.purchases),
      (SELECT MAX(end_date)       FROM stg.end_inventory)
    ) AS dmax
),
series AS (
  SELECT generate_series(dmin, dmax, interval '1 day')::date AS d
  FROM bounds
)
SELECT
  d                                         AS date_key,
  EXTRACT(YEAR  FROM d)::int                AS year,
  EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM d)::int              AS quarter,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM d)::int                AS month,
  EXTRACT(DAY   FROM d)::int                AS day,
  TO_CHAR(d,'YYYY-MM')                      AS year_month,
  TO_CHAR(d,'Dy')                           AS dow_short,
  EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM d)::int               AS dow_num,
  (EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM d) IN (6,7))         AS is_weekend
FROM series;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON mart.dim_date(date_key);



```

    1.2 dim_product
```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.dim_product;
CREATE TABLE mart.dim_product AS
WITH all_products AS (
  SELECT inventory_id, brand, size, description FROM stg.begin_inventory
  UNION ALL
  SELECT inventory_id, brand, size, description FROM stg.end_inventory
  UNION ALL
  SELECT inventory_id, brand, size, description FROM stg.sales
  UNION ALL
  SELECT inventory_id, brand, size, description FROM stg.purchases
),
cleaned AS (
  SELECT trim(inventory_id) AS inventory_id,
         NULLIF(trim(brand),'')       AS brand,
         NULLIF(trim(size),'')        AS size,
         NULLIF(trim(description),'') AS description
  FROM all_products
  WHERE inventory_id IS NOT NULL
),
dedup AS (
  SELECT
    inventory_id,
    MIN(brand)       AS brand,        -- fallback rule: pick alphabetically smallest non-null
    MIN(size)        AS size,
    MIN(description) AS description
  FROM cleaned
  GROUP BY inventory_id
)
SELECT * FROM dedup;

ALTER TABLE mart.dim_product ADD PRIMARY KEY (inventory_id);



```

    1.3 dim_store
```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.dim_store;
CREATE TABLE mart.dim_store AS
SELECT store_code,
       MIN(store_city) AS store_city   -- collapse duplicates
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT store_code, store_city FROM stg.begin_inventory
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT store_code, store_city FROM stg.end_inventory
) t
GROUP BY store_code;

ALTER TABLE mart.dim_store ADD PRIMARY KEY (store_code);
```

     1.4.1 See wht is causing the conflict: this finds all the vendor numbers that appear with multiple names across our staging tables.
```{sql}
WITH all_vendors AS (
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),'') AS vendor_number,
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')   AS vendor_name
  FROM stg.vendor_invoice
  UNION ALL
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),''),
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')
  FROM stg.purchases
  UNION ALL
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),''),
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')
  FROM stg.sales
)
SELECT vendor_number,
       COUNT(DISTINCT vendor_name) AS distinct_names,
       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT vendor_name) AS names_sample
FROM all_vendors
WHERE vendor_number IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY vendor_number
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vendor_name) > 1
ORDER BY distinct_names DESC, vendor_number
LIMIT 50;

-- the following vendor names berak the PK
-- 2 rows returned
-- vendor_number
-- text
-- distinct_names
-- bigint
-- names_sample
-- text[]
-- 1	1587	2	VINEYARD BRANDS INC,VINEYARD BRANDS LLC
-- 2	2000	2	SOUTHERN GLAZERS W&S OF NE,SOUTHERN WINE & SPIRITS NE
```

    1.4.2 Building a robust dim_vendor (dedupe +canonical name)
        assumption: postgres supports mode()
```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.dim_vendor;
CREATE TABLE mart.dim_vendor AS
WITH all_vendors AS (
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),'') AS vendor_number,
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')   AS vendor_name
  FROM stg.vendor_invoice
  UNION ALL
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),''),
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')
  FROM stg.purchases
  UNION ALL
  SELECT NULLIF(trim(vendor_number),''),
         NULLIF(trim(vendor_name),'')
  FROM stg.sales
),
clean AS (
  SELECT vendor_number, vendor_name
  FROM all_vendors
  WHERE vendor_number IS NOT NULL
),
dedup AS (
  SELECT
    vendor_number,
    -- pick the most frequent vendor_name; if tie/NULL, fallback to MIN
    COALESCE(
      mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY vendor_name),
      MIN(vendor_name)
    ) AS vendor_name
  FROM clean
  GROUP BY vendor_number
)
SELECT * FROM dedup;

ALTER TABLE mart.dim_vendor ADD PRIMARY KEY (vendor_number);



```



2. Facts
    2.1 fct_sales ( grain: date x store x product)

```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.fct_sales;
CREATE TABLE mart.fct_sales AS
SELECT
  s.sales_date                             AS date_key,
  s.store_code,
  s.inventory_id,
  COALESCE(s.sales_quantity, 0)            AS qty,
  COALESCE(s.sales_dollars,  0)::numeric(14,2) AS dollars,
  s.sales_price::numeric(12,2)             AS unit_price,   -- may be null if not provided
  COALESCE(s.excise_tax, 0)::numeric(12,2) AS excise_tax,
  s.vendor_number
FROM stg.sales s
WHERE s.sales_date IS NOT NULL;

-- helpful indexes
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_sales (date_key);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_sales (store_code);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_sales (inventory_id);



```

    2.2 fct_purchases (grain: PO x product )

```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.fct_purchases;
CREATE TABLE mart.fct_purchases AS
SELECT
  COALESCE(p.receiving_date, p.po_date, p.invoice_date) AS date_key,
  p.po_number,
  p.vendor_number,
  p.inventory_id,
  p.store_code,
  COALESCE(p.quantity, 0)                AS qty,
  COALESCE(p.dollars,  0)::numeric(14,2) AS dollars,
  p.purchase_price::numeric(12,2)        AS unit_price,
  p.classification
FROM stg.purchases p
WHERE COALESCE(p.receiving_date, p.po_date, p.invoice_date) IS NOT NULL;

CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_purchases (date_key);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_purchases (po_number);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_purchases (vendor_number);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_purchases (inventory_id);



```


    2.3 fct_inventory_snapshot (grain is snapshot_date x store x product )
```{sql}
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mart.fct_inventory_snapshot;
CREATE TABLE mart.fct_inventory_snapshot AS
SELECT
  b.start_date                             AS snapshot_date,
  b.store_code,
  b.inventory_id,
  b.on_hand_qty,
  b.unit_price,
  'begin'::text AS snapshot_type
FROM stg.begin_inventory b
WHERE b.start_date IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT
  e.end_date   AS snapshot_date,
  e.store_code,
  e.inventory_id,
  e.on_hand_qty,
  e.unit_price,
  'end'::text  AS snapshot_type
FROM stg.end_inventory e
WHERE e.end_date IS NOT NULL;

CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_inventory_snapshot (snapshot_date);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_inventory_snapshot (store_code);
CREATE INDEX ON mart.fct_inventory_snapshot (inventory_id);



```


3.  referential Sanity
```{sql}
-- rows in facts lacking a dimension match (expect 0 ideally)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing_products
FROM mart.fct_sales f
LEFT JOIN mart.dim_product d USING (inventory_id)
WHERE d.inventory_id IS NULL;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing_stores
FROM mart.fct_sales f
LEFT JOIN mart.dim_store s USING (store_code)
WHERE s.store_code IS NULL;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing_vendors
FROM mart.fct_purchases f
LEFT JOIN mart.dim_vendor v USING (vendor_number)
WHERE v.vendor_number IS NULL;
```

4. Quick "business views " for having handy analysis and dashboards
    4.1 Daily sales by store/product
```{sql}
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW mart.v_sales_daily AS
SELECT
  f.date_key,
  d.year, d.month, d.year_month,
  f.store_code,
  f.inventory_id,
  p.brand, p.description, p.size,
  SUM(f.qty)     AS qty,
  SUM(f.dollars) AS dollars
FROM mart.fct_sales f
JOIN mart.dim_date d    ON d.date_key = f.date_key
JOIN mart.dim_product p ON p.inventory_id = f.inventory_id
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8, p.size;


select * from mart.v_sales_daily limit 20;
```

    4.2 Vendor Performance (costs and invoices)

```{sql}
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW mart.v_vendor_costs AS
SELECT
  COALESCE(p.vendor_number, vi.vendor_number) AS vendor_number,
  v.vendor_name,
  d.year_month,
  SUM(p.qty)            AS purchased_qty,
  SUM(p.dollars)        AS purchase_dollars,
  SUM(vi.dollars)       AS invoiced_dollars,
  SUM(vi.freight)       AS freight_dollars,
  SUM(vi.dollars) - SUM(p.dollars) AS invoice_minus_po
FROM mart.fct_purchases p
FULL OUTER JOIN stg.vendor_invoice vi
  ON p.po_number = vi.po_number
     AND COALESCE(p.vendor_number, vi.vendor_number) = vi.vendor_number
JOIN mart.dim_vendor v
  ON v.vendor_number = COALESCE(p.vendor_number, vi.vendor_number)
LEFT JOIN mart.dim_date d
  ON d.date_key = COALESCE(p.date_key, vi.invoice_date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3;


select * from mart.v_vendor_costs limit 20;
```
